transcript: Morning Keith! How's the bakery this week — Alan keeping you on your toes? Listen, I've been meaning to ask you something.
Morning, Megan. Bakery's fine, busy enough. Alan's Alan. Go on, what is it?

It's about Craig, actually. He borrowed eight hundred off me a while back and I've not seen a penny of it. I don't want to fall out with him over it, but I'm getting a bit brassed off. You know him better than most — has he said anything to you about money troubles? I don't want to go in all guns blazing if he's struggling.

Craig? Not said a word to me about money, Megan. But he's not one to talk about it, is he. Eight hundred's a fair bit. I'd have a quiet word first, not in front of anyone. Go easy on him, he might be in a hole he's too proud to show.

That's good advice, Keith, I'll do that — catch him on his own sometime, no audience. I don't want to be the one who puts the boot in if he's skint. Anyway, enough of my troubles — how's things with you? How's the family keeping?

Fine, Megan, thanks for asking. Household's tight like everyone's, but we're getting by. Owen's working, Dave's on at the Corner Stores, so we're keeping our heads above water. Rent's going up again, which doesn't help, but there it is. How about you, you holding up alright?

transcript: Morning Dad — kettle's on, do you want a brew? I've been thinking about money again, the rent going up and all. Reckon I might have a chat with Sian at the bank about the loan.

Brew would be good, son. Sit down a minute. The rent's going up, aye, and I know it. Sian at the bank's fine, but don't go signing for more than we can carry. We're already sending forty-odd a week on the cards. Let's look at the numbers first, the two of us, before you ask her for anything.

Aye, fair enough — brew first, numbers second. I'll get the pad out and we can go through it proper: what's coming in, what's going out, and how much slack there really is before I go near Sian. I don't want to sign for anything daft either — the last thing we need is another card spiral.

Right, pad's here. Start with what's coming in. My pay's four sixty a week, Dave's draw from the Corner Stores is three eighty, and yours is four twenty. Write those down first, then we take the outgoings off it.

Right, so that's four sixty, three eighty, four twenty — call it twelve sixty a week coming in. Now the outgoings: rent's a hundred and seventy-five, bills two-fourteen, loan forty-three, food about a hundred and twenty-two. That's five fifty-four all told, so we've got the bones of seven hundred a week left over — doesn't feel so grim when you write it out. What else should we be putting on the list, Dad? Fuel, that sort of thing?

Fuel, aye, put it down. Fifteen a week, near enough, more if the car's been out to the depot. And the car's insurance, write that as a monthly figure, divide it by four and add it on. Then food. The hundred and twenty-two is what we spend on a normal week, not a good one, so don't go telling yourself we've got seven hundred spare. Put the cards down too, the forty-three is only the consolidation loan, the card minimums are on top of it, and I want those on the page before you say another word to Sian.
